notes.heading: Profit, cash and the timing of recognition
paragraphs: Revenue and cash receipts can occur at different times. When a service is supplied on credit, the receivable increases and the earned revenue contributes to profit; collecting that receivable later exchanges one asset for another. Treating collection as new revenue counts the same service twice. Borrowing increases cash and a liability without creating profit. Owner withdrawals reduce equity without becoming a business expense. Analyse each transaction first by the resource or obligation it changes, then check the equation. A balanced equation is necessary but does not prove that every transaction has been classified correctly.

questions.prompt: In a fictional service business with no sales tax, a service worth 600 units is completed on credit. The customer later pays 400. Give the entries for both events and the remaining receivable.
questions.answer: On completion: debit receivables 600 and credit service revenue 600. On collection: debit cash 400 and credit receivables 400. Receivables remaining: 200.
solution: Recognise the earned service once, creating revenue and a receivable.
Collection changes the composition of assets; 600 - 400 = 200 remains unpaid.

questions.prompt: A fictional sole trader withdraws 250 units of business cash for personal use. A student records wage expense 250. Correct the classification and explain the effect on profit and equity.
questions.answer: Debit drawings 250 and credit cash 250. The withdrawal reduces equity by 250 and does not reduce business profit.
solution: Identify the payment as an owner withdrawal rather than a cost of earning revenue.
Reverse the mistaken expense classification and record drawings.
markingPoints: Give debit drawings and credit cash.
Distinguish unchanged profit from reduced equity.

questions.prompt: A fictional business receives a 1,000-unit bank loan but credits revenue instead of the loan liability. Cash is correctly debited. Explain why the trial balance agrees and identify the misstatements.
questions.answer: Equal debit and credit entries still balance. Revenue and profit are overstated by 1,000; the loan liability is understated by 1,000.
solution: Compare the actual credit with the required liability credit.
The trial balance checks numerical equality, not the economic meaning of the account.
markingPoints: Explain equal debit and credit totals.
